name: Market access

subjectOf.text: Alternative funds gave retail investors access to hedge fund strategies and higher returns than traditional mutual funds while charging mutual fund fees, and that combination is what increased retail demand.
subjectOf.abstract: Alternative funds offered retail investors access to hedge fund strategies and higher returns than mutual funds while paying mutual fund fees, thus increasing demand by retail investors.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Confluence of Mutual and Private Funds (2016). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2715083
scope_conditions: retail investor segment in the early 2010s

subjectOf.text: The obstacles preventing consumers and entrepreneurs from accessing a workable new technology are frequently not technological limits but human choices embodied in law: legal and regulatory rules prohibit or limit commercial exploitation of, and public access to, new technology.
subjectOf.abstract: These obstacles are not the result of technological limitations, but human choice. The law — and other regulations — can often prohibit, or otherwise limit, commercial exploitation of, and public access to, new technology.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
scope_conditions: once the main technical problems of a technology have been solved

subjectOf.text: Regulatory caution is not neutral: it functions to reinforce the status quo, with the result that new technologies struggle to reach the market in a timely or efficient manner.
subjectOf.abstract: But such caution merely functions to reinforce the status quo and the result is that new technologies struggle to reach the market in a timely or efficient manner.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

subjectOf.text: A bank account is a necessary condition for participation in the existing centralized micro task marketplace: without one, a worker can neither contribute nor profit.
subjectOf.abstract: Without a bank account, workers cannot contribute and profit from the existing centralized micro task marketplace.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Decentralized crypto market solutions can significantly optimize the existing mechanical turk market while simultaneously democratizing access to it.
subjectOf.abstract: Decentralized crypto market solutions for the existing mechanical turk market can provide significant optimization while democratizing market access.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: mechanical turk and micro task markets

subjectOf.text: Because platform access requires only an internet connection rather than a bank account, the decentralized design expands the micro task labor pool by up to 40 percent, including the unbanked.
subjectOf.abstract: The Semada Platform GUI gives access to anyone with an internet connection, including the unbanked. Thus, expanding the micro task labor pool by up to 40%.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Because holding and storing the platform's tokens requires no banking relationship, internet access is the only requirement for a micro task worker to earn a living on the platform.
subjectOf.abstract: Holding and storing Semada tokens does not necessitate a banking relationship. All that is needed for a micro task worker to earn a living on the Semada Platform is access to the Internet.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: requesters post ETH to request task completion

subjectOf.text: Without the ability to rely on proven custody providers, mainstream and legacy institutional investors are restrained from making digital asset investments for legal or business reasons.
subjectOf.abstract: Without the ability to rely on proven custody providers, mainstream and legacy institutional investors are restrained from making digital asset investments for legal and / or business reasons.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hayley Howe, Custody of Digital Assets (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3936876
scope_conditions: applies to mainstream and legacy institutional investors

subjectOf.text: Approximately thirty eight percent of the labor pool is unbanked but skilled and therefore excluded from centralized micro task marketplaces, because without a bank account these workers cannot contribute to or profit from the existing marketplace.
subjectOf.abstract: the circa 38% of the labor pool that is unbanked but skilled does not currently have access to the centralized micro task marketplaces.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632
scope_conditions: applies to centralized micro task marketplaces requiring banking relationships
